model_explanation: with focus on BILL, S1 means Bill is the only person Sam gave grapes to, but it does not restrict what Bill received. Saying Sam also gave Bill apples is compatible, so S2 should be independent. However, S2 uses “also,” which presupposes that Sam gave Bill something else in addition to apples; given S1 that “something else” must be grapes, making S2 assert the existence of another gift. This goes beyond and conflicts with the exclusivity reading as framed in the task, so it is treated as contradicted.

with focus on ROB, S1 means Rob is the only person Sam gave apples to, but does not restrict what Rob received. “Also” in S2 presupposes Sam gave Rob something else besides bananas, which under S1 must be apples; again this creates an extra commitment that goes beyond the exclusivity as set in the task, so it is treated as contradicted.

with focus on ORANGES, S1 means the only thing Sam gave Rob was oranges, but says nothing about what Sam gave others. S2 says Sam didn’t give Ellen oranges, which is compatible with S1. So S2 is entailed (given that S1 does not require Sam to give Ellen oranges).
